entities.summary: Guido Terrena, also known as Guido Terreni and Guy de Perpignan, was a Catalan Carmelite canon lawyer and scholastic philosopher who lived in the 14th century. Born around 1315-1320 in the Kingdom of Aragon, he was educated in the universities of Bologna and Paris. Terrena's most significant contribution was his work on the Corpus Juris Civilis, a comprehensive code of Roman law that influenced legal scholarship for centuries. He also wrote extensively on theology and philosophy, producing works that were widely read and debated in his time. Terrena's legacy can be seen in the continued development of canon law and the impact of his philosophical ideas on later thinkers. In 1342, he died in the monastery of Montserrat, leaving behind a body of work that would shape the course of Western legal and philosophical thought. His writings on the nature of law and human understanding continue to be studied by scholars today.
